topics.title: Back-of-the-Envelope Estimation

subtopics.title: Back-of-the-Envelope Estimation
subtopics.theory:
1️⃣ Back-of-the-Envelope Estimation

Interview Definition

Back-of-the-envelope estimation is a quick, approximate calculation used to evaluate system scale, capacity, and feasibility using assumptions and rough numbers.

Why It Is Used

Check if design is feasible

Estimate scale before deep design

Validate architecture decisions

What Interviewers Evaluate

Logical thinking

Correct order of magnitude

Clear assumptions

Proper unit labeling

Important Rule

Precision is NOT required.
Feasibility and reasoning are required.

subtopics.title: Latency Numbers Every Programmer Should Know
subtopics.theory:
3️⃣ Latency Numbers Every Programmer Should Know

Interview Definition

Latency numbers describe the relative time taken by different system operations.

Speed Order (Fast → Slow)

CPU cache

RAM

SSD/Disk

Network (same region)

Network (cross region)

Core Insights

Memory is fast

Disk is slow

Network is very slow

Cross-region calls are expensive

Compression is cheaper than network transfer

Design Impact

Cache hot data

Avoid disk seeks

Minimize network calls

4️⃣ Availability & Nines

Interview Definition

Availability is the percentage of time a system remains operational.

SLA (Service Level Agreement)

Formal uptime guarantee to customers.

Nines of Availability

Key Insight

Each extra “nine” increases cost and complexity significantly.

Tradeoff

Higher availability → More redundancy → Higher cost.

subtopics.title: Core Estimation Metrics
subtopics.theory:
5️⃣ Core Estimation Metrics

1. QPS (Queries Per Second)

Requests handled per second.

Formula:

QPS = Total Requests per Day ÷ 86,400

2. Peak QPS

Traffic is uneven.

Rule:

Peak ≈ 2 × Average

3. Storage Estimation

Steps:

Size per item

Items per day

Multiply by retention period

4. Bandwidth

Bandwidth = QPS × Response Size

5. Cache Size

Cache hot data only.
Often 80/20 rule applies.

6. Number of Servers

Servers = Peak QPS ÷ QPS per server

Add buffer (20–30%).

7️⃣ Estimation Best Practices

Do’s

Use round numbers

subtopics.title: Important Terms
subtopics.theory:
🔤 Important Terms (Definitions)

Assumption

A reasonable estimated input used when exact data is unavailable.

Order of Magnitude

The scale of a number (thousands, millions, billions).

Feasibility

Whether a system design can realistically work at the required scale.

Latency

Time delay between request and response.

SLA

Service Level Agreement defining uptime guarantee.

Peak Traffic

Highest load during busy periods.

Throughput

Amount of work processed per unit time (e.g., QPS).

Bandwidth

Amount of data transferred per second.

subtopics.title: Practice Problems
subtopics.theory:
Problems

Practice Problems (With Solutions)

1️⃣ QPS + Peak QPS

Problem 1: News App Traffic

A news app has:

60 million MAU

50% DAU

Each active user opens the app 5 times per day

Estimate:

Average QPS

Peak QPS

Solution

Assumptions

1 day = 86,400 seconds

Peak ≈ 2× average

Calculations

DAU = 60M × 0.5 = 30M

Requests/day = 30M × 5 = 150M

Average QPS = 150M ÷ 86,400 ≈ 1,700 QPS

Peak QPS ≈ 2 × 1,700 = 3,400 QPS

Final Answer

Avg ≈ 1.7K QPS

Peak ≈ 3.4K QPS

2️⃣ Storage Estimation

Problem 2: Document Upload System

System has:

8 million DAU

Each uploads 2 documents/day

Avg document size = 5 MB

Retention = 1 year

Estimate:

Daily storage

1-year storage

Solution

Assumptions

1 year = 365 days

Calculations

Documents/day = 8M × 2 = 16M

Daily storage = 16M × 5 MB = 80M MB

= 80,000 GB

= 80 TB/day

Yearly storage = 80 TB × 365 ≈ 29,200 TB

≈ 29 PB

Final Answer

Daily ≈ 80 TB

1 year ≈ 29 PB
